## a test filter
🎯 Test Filter: Mem-Mirror*,Lat-L3-*
  Running tests matching pattern
  Default: cycles=1 for quick targeted runs
  CLI overrides supported (e.g. duration=60 cycles=5)

## the quick test
🚀 TMR Quick Test Mode: plan=quick, the stability tests once
  Quick test uses reduced memory (60% reserve) for faster validation
  CLI overrides supported

## every parameter note
  Minimum Page Size: regular
  Maximum Page Size: large
  hugechunk: 2GiB
  blkround: down
  Topology Detection: windowsv2
  CPU Pinning: skip-cores=0
  CPU Pinning: Disabled
## the header of a release build
Startup Mode & Parameters:
  Command Line: tmr.exe memory=50% cputype=cores cpus=100% skip-cores=0 cycles=1
  Build Type: ✅ Release (optimized)
## the header of a debug build
Startup Mode & Parameters:
  Command Line: tmr.exe
  Build Type: ❌ Debug (unoptimized)
## the parameters, given and defaults
  RUST_LOG: info
  Explicit Parameters: memory=50%, --startup-debug
  Default Parameters: cputype=threads (default), errors=log (default)
## the parameters, a backtrace set and none given
  RUST_LOG: debug
  RUST_BACKTRACE: 1
## cores
  CPU Type: cores (avoiding SMT/Hyperthreading)
## threads
  CPU Type: threads
## a share of the CPUs
  CPU Count: 50% of 6 available = 3 thread(s)
## pinned, a core skipped, SMT doubling avoided, both limits
  Error Mode: Log and continue
  Using 3/5 cores for testing
  CPU Assignment: [2, 4, 6]
  Skipping core 5, the last in the core order (skip-cores=1), for system responsiveness
  Avoiding SMT doubling (using physical cores only)
  Test Suite Timing: 3 cycles or 600s max (whichever first)
  SIMD Support: SSE, SSE2, SSE3, SSE4.1, SSE4.2, AVX, AVX2

## unpinned, halting, cycles only
  Error Mode: Halt on first error
  Using 3/6 cores for testing
  CPU Assignment: [2, 4, 6] ⚠️ NUMA placement only, pinning is off
  Test Suite Timing: 1 cycles (no time limit)
  SIMD Support: SSE, SSE2, SSE3, SSE4.1, SSE4.2, AVX, AVX2

## panicking, time only, a share skipped
  Error Mode: Panic on error (debug mode)
  Using 3/4 cores for testing
  CPU Assignment: [2, 4, 6]
  Skipping cores 0 and 5, the last in the core order (skip-cores=25%), for system responsiveness
  Test Suite Timing: 60s duration (unlimited cycles)
  SIMD Support: SSE, SSE2, SSE3, SSE4.1, SSE4.2, AVX, AVX2

## no limits, a core range left out
  Error Mode: Log and continue
  Using 3/4 cores for testing
  CPU Assignment: [2, 4, 6]
  Skipping cores 4 and 5 (skip-cores=4-5)
  Test Suite Timing: Unlimited cycles and duration
  SIMD Support: SSE, SSE2, SSE3, SSE4.1, SSE4.2, AVX, AVX2

## large pages are checked
Checking Large Page access
## the right granted
✅ Granted 'Lock pages in memory' (SeLockMemoryPrivilege) to BUILTIN\Administrators, which keeps it until it is removed
🔄 SIGN-IN REQUIRED: sign out and back in (or restart Windows) for it to take effect, then run TMR again

To sign out: Start Menu → your account → Sign out
To restart:
  • Windows: shutdown /r /t 0
  • Or use Start Menu → Power → Restart

TMR will exit now.
## the grant failed
❌ Couldn't grant 'Lock pages in memory' (SeLockMemoryPrivilege) to PC\owner: LsaAddAccountRights: Access is denied. (5, NTSTATUS 0xC0000022)

📖 Manual Setup:
1. Run gpedit.msc as Administrator (Windows Pro and up: Home has none)
2. Navigate to: Computer Configuration → Windows Settings → Security Settings → Local Policies → User Rights Assignment
3. Double-click 'Lock pages in memory'
4. Add PC\owner
5. Sign out and back in (or restart Windows)

## what the check did
🔍 Large Page Diagnostic
  Privilege: assigned and enabled
  Test allocation: 2 MiB, succeeded
## large pages usable
🎉 Large Pages: ✅ ENABLED and tested successfully!
   TMR will use 2MB large pages for optimal performance

## large pages not usable, and minpage needs them
⚠️  Large Pages: Not available, and minpage=large needs them, so the run will stop
   before allocating. Set them up (tmr.exe --setup-large-pages, elevated), or rerun
   with minpage=regular to test on standard 4KB pages: every test still runs, but
   slower memory traffic is less stress, so marginal errors that only appear at
   full bandwidth may go undetected

## large pages not usable, and minpage doesn't need them
⚠️  Large Pages: Not available - TMR will use standard 4KB pages
   Performance impact: ~5-10% slower memory allocation
   Every test still runs and every pattern is still checked, but slower
   memory traffic is less stress, so marginal errors that only appear at
   full bandwidth may go undetected

  Calibration: Loaded (2026-10-20 09:05)
## no cache calibration
  Calibration: none stored: measured on this run's memory before its tests, about 2 minutes

  Calibration: the one stored is another machine's: measured before the tests, about 2 minutes
## one measured one thread only
  Calibration: the one stored measured one thread only: measured again with the others running, before the tests
## calibrate=always
  Calibration: measured before the tests, about 2 minutes (calibrate=always)
## calibrate=recheck
  Calibration: Loaded (2026-10-20 09:05), rechecked before the tests, about 15 s (calibrate=recheck)
## the cache calibration off
  Calibration: off (calibrate=off): sizes from CPUID
## the seal calibration
  Seal calibration: Loaded (256 bits, 2026-10-21 09:05)
## another machine's seal calibration
  Seal calibration: Stale (hardware changed, re-run --calibrate-seal)
## no seal calibration
  Seal calibration: None (run --calibrate-seal to calibrate)

## realtime on every CPU
⚠️  priority=realtime with a worker on every logical CPU: the console and input can freeze until the run ends. Leave a core free (skip-cores=1) or use priority=high.
## the default plan
📋 Plan: stability (the default): the stability tests at the widest width
## a plan named
📋 Plan: quick: the stability tests once
## the tests start
Starting comprehensive memory tests... Use CTRL+C for graceful shutdown with final report
(more here with RUST_LOG=info or debug; the log file takes info either way)
